result.summary: Makes the `.onion` suffix check case-insensitive when parsing network addresses in `CNetAddr::SetTor`. This aligns Tor address parsing with existing I2P hostname handling and prevents addresses with uppercase `.ONION` suffixes from falling through to regular DNS hostname resolution.
result.problem: Tor addresses containing uppercase letters in the `.onion` suffix are not recognized as Tor addresses. Instead, they fail `SetTor` and fall through to standard DNS hostname resolution, risking privacy leaks or connection failures.
evidence: PR description: 'With the current code, a name like <addr>.ONION will not be parsed as a Tor address, and will instead fall through to regular hostname resolution.'
result.changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete diff and test coverage (a new unit test in `src/test/net_tests.cpp` validating mixed-case Tor address parsing); implementation logic remains the same.
result.card: Makes the suffix check case-insensitive when parsing .onion network addresses, matching existing behavior for I2P hostnames. Currently, hostnames ending in uppercase variations like .ONION fail Tor address detection and fall through to regular DNS resolution. This prevents potential DNS leaks and connection failures when configuring or parsing mixed-case Tor addresses.

risk.why: A flaw in netaddress parsing could misparse network addresses or fail to identify Tor destinations, but the change is tiny, localized, and well-covered by unit tests.
